title: Sequences and lists
description: Lists as the primary fixed/dynamic sequence

exercises.title: Create Array
exercises.description: Create an array of 5 ints with values 1,2,3,4,5. Print all elements.
hints: Use `int[] arr = {1,2,3,4,5};` and a small helper to print `[1 2 3 4 5]` like the solution’s `fmt` method.
`Arrays.toString` uses commas — bracket spacing must match the exercise.

exercises.title: Array Iteration
exercises.description: Create array nums = [10, 20, 30}. Use range to System.out.println each element.

exercises.title: Array Length
exercises.description: Create arr = [1, 2, 3, 4}. Print the length using len(arr).

exercises.title: Partial Array Initialization
exercises.description: Create an array of 5 ints where only the first two are initialized to 10 and 20. Print the array.
hints: After partially filling `new int[5]`, format with the same bracket style as `arrays_01`.

exercises.title: 2D Array
exercises.description: Create a 2x2 matrix with values {{1, 2}, {3, 4}}. Print each element on separate lines.
hints: Nested loops: outer over rows, inner over each row’s elements.

exercises.title: Array Sum
exercises.description: Create arr = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50}. Compute the sum of all elements and System.out.println it.
hints: Accumulate with `int sum = 0;` and `for (int v : arr) sum += v;`.

exercises.title: Array Element Access
exercises.description: Create arr = [100, 200, 300}. Print the first element (index 0) and last element (index 2).
